class: Regular bounded Architecture qualification. The new question concerns the capacity of the convex reconstruction class and information in the observation, independently of the WL106 coverage-moment mechanism.
hypothesis: The existing inputs contain usable grazing-rim information, but convex LOW/HIGH spatial averaging or its learned weight prediction cannot exploit it without a significant bias–variance trade-off.

provenance.WL105: a3c4069 with protocol freeze 42f386c and seed amendment dda00cd; complete original raw hash anchors in evaluation/105/raw_manifest105.json
provenance.WL106: a29d629 closure; 10892c0 protocol freeze; SG2 failed and R4 untrained; synthetic106.json and manifest106.json kept as historical controls
provenance.WL103: 04a93e7; original normal-arm covariance evidence, frozen protocol id WL101H

controls.C0_C1: Validate the complete WL105 train/val/eval file set, checkpoints and stored predictions against the archived hashes and rerun R0–R3 for every frozen evaluation input. Per-image relative L1 <= 1e-6; compare pre/post input tensors, and repeat one inference bitwise. Verify archived renderer replays at 4096 spp against WL105 tolerances.
controls.C2_C3: Analytic integral and independent subpixel integration checks; report bias, squared bias, variance, RMSE, cross-boundary energy and residual profile independently.
controls.C4: Fit the full local RGB LOW/HIGH covariance factor from independent joint whole-frame draws. Retain both cross-component and cross-tap terms. Report empirical evaluation LOW, HIGH, 2Cov, TOTAL and verify closure. Exact structured covariance for synthetic continuous cases.
controls.C5: Same 40/8/6 camera split and 4/16/32 spp. Train only on original training files, log validation only. O1 target, covariance, and evaluation observations have disjoint streams. No eval or validation supervision for O2.
controls.C6: 46 fresh independent 8192-spp blocks plus the two WL105 halves for each assessment target; eight separate fresh 8192-spp blocks for O1 fitting. Reuse original renderer and definitions. Measure standard error from the variance across 48 blocks. Target noise <= 10% of smallest eligible-arm relative RMSE for each decision ROI and spp. Also require assessment reference signed-luminance SE <= 0.25 percentage points in each occupied decision stratum. A failing precision cell cannot support a verdict.
controls.C7: O0 repeats the WL105 GPU timing contract. Any O4 must measure synchronized end-to-end and reconstruction latency, peak memory, parameter count and cost-matched quality under WL105 interpolation; historical timing and O2 diagnostic timing are tagged separately.

arms.O0: Frozen R3; R0/R1/R2 reproduced as provenance and context.
arms.O1: Per-pixel risk-minimizing two-simplex fixed kernels, one 225-tap reflect-padded weight vector for each of LOW and HIGH, shared across RGB. Fit with privileged mean and covariance; report lower bounds on empirical convex objectives using the first-order simplex gap. Joint TOTAL bias and variance are optimized at variance multipliers [0.03125, 0.125, 0.5, 1, 2, 8, 32]. A samplewise LUMA interval yields a separate optimistic lower bound valid even for noise-dependent weights; a fixed-weight miss alone does not exclude adaptive kernels. Count nonconverged bounds as unresolved.
arms.O2: Diagnostic only: R3 architecture with its actual log1p(LOW) or log1p(HIGH) plus all 14 unchanged guides, same 1,055,624 trainable parameters, shared RGB kernel, reflect padding and component loss. Relax nonnegativity with weights softmax(logits) + (logits - mean(logits))/225, retaining unit sum. Same WL105 seed, initialization, exact crops, Adam recipe, 20000 steps and final checkpoint. No access to fit/assessment targets, camera IDs or privileged guides while training. The comparison diagnoses this relaxation and recipe, not all possible predictors.
arms.O3: Conditional ambiguity control. If O2 alone cannot resolve information vs learning, run matched Bayes estimators on the analytically specified equal-guide normal-mixture pair. The richer scalar is the foreground subpixel mean squared view-normal cosine (geometry only). Equal scenes and priors, exact conditional means. Report observation overlap and irreducible errors. This control diagnoses finite-atom ambiguity in the synthetic family only, and cannot settle real-scene insufficiency. If real ambiguity persists, a matched real diagnostic may be run once with this scalar generated by the same frozen 8x8 camera intersections, using a reserved input shared by O2 control and O3 and an identical WL105 budget; stop before any production representation change.
arms.O4: Conditional on a specific localized operator defect, existing-input sufficiency under the full target/safety contract, and no need to change the renderer or input representation. Freeze one mechanism in a dated addendum before training/final evaluation. Requires same recipe, safety, cost and synthetic validation. No automatic adoption.

synthetic.geometry: 64-square analytic vertical box-filtered silhouettes, offsets [0.125, 0.3, 0.5, 0.875], foreground on the positive signed-distance side; piecewise constant, smooth ramp, dark rim at widths [0.25, 1, 3] pixels, flat and wavy tangential radiance, bright and inverted foreground/background contrast. Include zero-coverage, mixed and near-full rows. Preserve the complete published WL106 SG2 thin-strip and SG3 controls as read-only evidence. Separately include a single isolated dark pixel with a balanced two-atom center observation, and a collision in the observation induced by a foreground normal mixture.
synthetic.truth: Analytic uniform pixel area integrals of piecewise-linear/exponential radiance, checked against independent dense midpoint integration. Quantized 8x8 midpoint coverage and mean normal/depth simulate the input guides. Synthetic RGB colors and LOW/HIGH partition are declared in code. Noise is nonnegative-support additive joint bounded zero-mean noise with calibrated component cross-covariance and a shared frame term to test spatial covariance; evaluate 256 independent draws per spp, plus exact moments.
synthetic.counterexamples: Equal-guide two-world probe has symmetric unit normals with m=0.5 in the view direction. World A uses cosine 0.5 throughout, world B equal 0.2/0.8. The analytic nonlinear radiance response has a rare atom only in B; enumerate binomial probabilities at 4/16/32 spp. On all-zero-response, the entire observed footprint can be identical while targets differ. Different unconditional means imply different full sampling distributions.
synthetic.acceptance: Reference/constraint test failures stop. A synthetic capacity miss is an experiment outcome. Use per-case signed band bias <= 1%, band row/profile RMS bias <= 1%, and >= 50% variance reduction vs raw at a frozen spp; per-case residuals shown without excluding any workload. The isolated extremum tests a separate adaptive lower bound analytically.

real.workload: All V0 and H1–H5, eight frozen independent observations per spp. O1 uses all silhouette pixels for interval bounds and a fixed panel of up to 32 per coverage bin per view for full covariance convex optimization and comparisons against identical O0 panel pixels. For each bin select uniformly spaced row-major indices; use all if <=32.
real.roi: WL105 geometry masks intersected with its contact-exclusion complement for every decision ROI. Keep raw contact observations separate, with no attribution. WL106 sphere-coverage bin edges (a bin with >=20 pixels per view qualifies), signed-distance profile extending 7 pixels each side, and per-view reports. Depth/normal summaries use the unchanged aux fields on panel and entire rim.
real.metrics: WL105 mean relative RGB RMSE, signed luminance bias and gradient ratio. Luminance and RGB inter-seed variance, squared bias of the replicate mean, component covariance closure, conditional residual profiles, boundary-band side redistribution. For O1 report analytic fitted risk, solver lower bound, out-of-fit risk and variance; adaptive luminance lower bound is compared in luminance units. No oracle speed claim.
real.significance: Retain WL106 1% signed bias and [0.8,1.2] silhouette gradient safety, >=50% reduction of absolute silhouette bias vs R3 (95% interval lower bound above zero), primary relative RMSE ratio <=1.02 (upper 95% <=1.05), silhouette/material boundary <=1.05. A meaningful variance reduction is >=50% against raw, with a ratio upper 95% <=0.50 for learned conclusions. O1 panel uses <=1% pooled signed bias and <=1% coverage-binned profile RMS bias plus >=50% sample variance reduction; panel safety is an oracle diagnostic rather than whole-image qualification.
real.statistics: 10,000 paired replicates via resampling held-out views and original draws within each view. For across-seed variance resampling, recenter the resampled covariance estimate or use a view-cluster interval; report method. Keep signed sides separate so cancellation is visible. Target-block SE is estimated independently of the evaluation draws.
real.verdict: A fixed-weight limitation is scoped to fixed kernels. For the real adaptive class require a qualified samplewise lower bound or equivalent certificate violating a required risk constraint. Input-information limitation needs a controlled observation ambiguity; a failed O2 is optimizer/training confounded. Synthetic controlled findings cannot by themselves drive a real-scene Architecture verdict. Qualify existing-input success only with held-out safety, variance and quality at each of the three spp.

seeds.covariance_32spp: 11720000 + 1000 * view + draw (0..63); covariance scaled by 32/spp, checked against spans of archived raw variance
seeds.launch: seed * 1000003 + launch_index; use the original 32 spp launch layout

budget: LabServer63; 324 fresh 8192-spp blocks and 384 independent 32-spp covariance draws maximum. Up to 4.25 GPU-hours for replay/reference/covariance, 30 GPU-min per authorized diagnostic fit, and 60 GPU-min for oracle/evaluation. 12 CPU core-hours for synthetic controls. Guard execution using the stage elapsed-time caps. No seed, target, threshold or case selection after inspecting evidence.
stop: Stop dependent evidence on failed replay, hash or split check, invalid analytic reference, incorrect oracle constraints, exhausted budget, unqualified target precision, or need to change production inputs/renderer. Archive failed evidence with the failed rule. Historical WL105/WL106 evidence retains original conclusions.
